executive_summary: scripts/adam-startup-check.mjs's contract-parity guard stacked three independent failures: its own parseDurableDutyMarkers regex only recognized a bare "(durable)" marker while solomon-startup-check.mjs's parser (already broadened under SD-LEO-INFRA-SOLOMON-STARTUP-PARITY-RECALIBRATE-001) accepts the qualifier form "(durable; <note>)"; its test file (tests/unit/adam-startup-check.test.mjs) uses node:test/node:assert directly, so vitest's --project unit never collected it and none of its 23 assertions were ever load-bearing in CI; and neither the qualifier-form case nor the existing zero-marker CONTRACT DRIFT guard in renderContractParity had any test coverage. The fix, delivered as Quick-Fix QF-20260903-433 and merged via PR #8674 (commit ab483f2889b) BEFORE this SD existed, reconciles Adam's parser onto Solomon's shared implementation (the same precedent michael-startup-check.mjs already follows), wires the test file into CI via a dedicated `node --test` step (mirroring the existing test:session-tick / test:adam-github-assessment pattern), and adds the two missing regression tests. This SD exists only because the diff touched a sensitive CI-workflow path (.github/workflows/unit-tier.yml) that complete-quick-fix.js's QF_ELIGIBILITY_PREFLIGHT refuses to self-close without a full SD, by design, with no bypass flag -- it is a retroactive verification record of an already-shipped, already-tested, already-merged fix, re-derived fresh from the repo at HEAD rather than accepted from the commit message.

functional_requirements.title: Reconcile Adam's durable-duty-marker parser onto Solomon's shared implementation
functional_requirements.description: scripts/adam-startup-check.mjs must no longer define its own parseDurableDutyMarkers regex. It imports parseDurableDutyMarkers and slugifyDuty from ./solomon-startup-check.mjs (the same pattern scripts/michael-startup-check.mjs already follows) and re-exports them so its own importers (including its test file) see no path change. Solomon's regex (/\*\*\s*([^*]+?)\s+DUTY\s*\(\s*durable\b[^)]*\)\s*[.:;,]?\s*\*\*/gi) accepts both the bare "(durable)" form and the qualifier form "(durable; <note>)".
acceptance_criteria: scripts/adam-startup-check.mjs:37 imports parseDurableDutyMarkers/slugifyDuty from ./solomon-startup-check.mjs; no local regex definition remains.
parseDurableDutyMarkers('**PLAN-ALIGNMENT REVIEW DUTY (durable; chairman-ratified 2026-07-20, heavy-now / light-later)**') returns ['plan-alignment-review'].
All 7 other vitest suites that import from adam-startup-check.mjs or solomon-startup-check.mjs (152 tests) pass unchanged -- the shared-import refactor introduces no regression.

Add a test:adam-startup-check npm script (node --test tests/unit/adam-startup-check.test.mjs) and a dedicated step in .github/workflows/unit-tier.yml, mirroring the existing test:session-tick and test:adam-github-assessment precedent in the same workflow file.

functional_requirements.title: Add regression coverage for the qualifier-form parse and the zero-marker CONTRACT DRIFT guard
functional_requirements.description: Add a test asserting a qualifier-form duty (e.g. '**PLAN-ALIGNMENT REVIEW DUTY (durable; ...)**') parses via parseDurableDutyMarkers AND resolves correctly through the consumer-side missingDurableDuties(md, ADAM_LOOPS). Add a negative test asserting a >1000-character fixture contract with zero durable markers causes renderContractParity to report CONTRACT DRIFT, never a silent CLEAN (the existing QF-20260828-890 guard inside renderContractParity had no test at all before this SD, despite the guard itself predating it).
acceptance_criteria: A test named for QF-20260903-433 asserts the qualifier-form duty parses to the expected slug and is resolved (present, not missing) against an ADAM_LOOPS entry with that key.

A test named for QF-20260903-433 builds a >1000-char zero-marker fixture, calls renderContractParity(dir), and asserts the output matches /CONTRACT DRIFT/ and does NOT match /all durable .* duties present/.
